history.summary: UNVERIFIED IDENTITY: no web footprint found for a 'Jagannath Prabhu Temple' in Churachandpur town/district - no map listing, directory entry, or news mention. Churachandpur (Lamka) is overwhelmingly Christian and its documented Hindu shrines are few. POSSIBLE DUPLICATE / CONFLATION: Manipur's famous Jagannath temple is the Jagannath section of the Shri Govindajee Temple in Imphal, built by Maharaja Churachand in 1908 (already covered as seq 705, whose CSV town/state were corrected to Imphal, Manipur) - the 'Churachandpur' town may be a garble of the king's name 'Churachand'. A separate 'Jaganath Temple' is listed by Justdial at Thiyam Leikai, NH-2, Bishnupur - a different district. This file is a thin placeholder; confirm locally before treating it as a distinct site.

name: Jagannath Prabhu Temple
town_description: Churachandpur, also called Lamka, is the second-largest town in Manipur and the headquarters of Churachandpur district, about 60 km southwest of Imphal on the Tiddim Road. It is the main urban centre of the hill tribes (Kuki-Zo communities) and is overwhelmingly Christian; Hindu shrines are few and small. The district borders Myanmar and the town serves as the region's principal market and administrative hub.

travel.airport: Imphal International Airport (IMF), ~60-65 km by Tiddim Road (verify)
travel.railway: No railway station in the district; nearest railheads are Dimapur (Nagaland) and Silchar (Assam), 150+ km away (verify)
travel.road: Tiddim Road (NH-102B) through Churachandpur/Lamka town, ~60 km southwest of Imphal (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, the dry, cool season
